correctness.rationale: Global phase and argument rotation uniquely set the first two coefficients to 1. For w=V/U, Parseval applied to P_m^4 splits into blocks [mj,mj+4]. In the separated-block Laurent polynomial the phase exponent difference is at most two, and the second harmonic comes only from j=2, exponent offset 2, with coefficient 6²=36. At w=1 the sum of squared binomial coefficients gives 70²=4900. At w=−1 the circle averages of |1+z|^(8−2j)|1−z|^(2j) are 70,10,6,10,70; multiplying by the corresponding squared binomial weights gives 676. These fix the remaining Laurent coefficients and yield 2644+2112 Re(w)+144 Re(w)², strictly increasing in Re(w). At m=4 the four adjacent overlaps add 2 Re(UK(w)), with coefficients 4,24,24,4. For h=|1+w| the absolute value is 4h(h²+3); maximizing or minimizing in U therefore yields the stated two envelopes. The upper envelope increases to 5012. The lower derivative divided by 24 is the strictly increasing cubic 6h³−h²+76h−1, with its root in (0,1/75) and a value strictly below 676 at h=1/76. Equality forces the stated unique U for each of the two w values. The normalized torus is connected, so there are no gaps in the ranges. The primitive cubic is irreducible by the rational-root bound and is not monic, so ρ is not integral; a root of unity w would make ρ²=2+w+w^(-1), hence ρ, integral. Normalizing root-of-unity phases retains root-of-unity phases. Binary phases have minimum 676. Frequency differences in |P_m|^8 are at most 4(m+1), verifying the stated finite-sampling condition.
residual_risks: The exact endpoint is the algebraic expression, not the printed decimal. Other supports, variable magnitudes, and lower sampling cutoffs are not claimed.
